comment: Open Access for Low- and Middle-Income Countries DPI-H is explicitly designed to support countries at all stages of digital health maturity, with particular focus on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The framework's Terminology Service requirement must therefore be achievable without prohibitive licensing costs. We note that an open access pathway already exists across our two organisations' standards, and we recommend that the DPI-H framework make this explicit: ● SNOMED International's SNOMED CT Global Patient Set (GPS) is freely available to all countries regardless of membership status, providing a clinically curated subset of SNOMED CT for use in LMIC settings without licensing cost. Corrections on inaccurately stated GPS information within the DPI-H will be submitted in the formal SNOMED International individual response. ● LOINC is available at no charge under an open license, It is available for use in commercial and non-commercial in accordance with terms of use provisions. ● UCUM is available at no charge under an open license available for use in commercial and non-commercial in accordance with terms of use provisions. We recommend Section 3.4.5 and the REDDHI Open Standards annex include explicit reference to the GPS as the LMIC-accessible entry point for SNOMED CT, and that the Licensing footnote (currently footnote 47 in the draft) be expanded to articulate the full open access pathway across SNOMED CT and LOINC. Conclusion Regenstrief and SNOMED International steward terminology and interoperability standards collectively used in over 80 countries and deployed in hundreds of millions of patient records worldwide. We have each independently arrived at a shared conviction: the DPI-H framework is a significant and timely contribution to global health informatics, and it deserves a robust, internationally coordinated implementation architecture. In this letter, we do not write to advocate for the interests of any single organisation. We write to offer the collective technical capacity of the global health standards community, freely and in partnership, to help WHO and ITU translate this ambitious framework into working national infrastructure. We would welcome the opportunity to meet with the DPI-H technical team at a mutually convenient time to discuss this response in depth, and we stand ready to contribute to any joint technical working group WHO and ITU may convene. We submit this response in the spirit of the collaborative, multilateral, open-standards approach that DPI-H itself espouses. Respectfully submitted, SNOMED International ____________________________ Don Sweete, Chief Executive Officer SNOMED International [email removed] Regenstrief Institute (LOINC) ____________________________ Marjorie Rallins, Executive Director, Health Data Standards Regenstrief Institute [email removed] This response is submitted to the WHO/ITU DPI-H public consultation. It represents the collective views of SNOMED International and the Regenstrief Institute with support from HL7 International. It does not constitute the individual policy positions of any single member organisation of HL7 International or the membership of SNOMED International. Enquiries may be directed to the contacts below. SNOMED International contact: Kelly Kuru, Chief Executive Communications & Collaborations | [email removed] Regenstrief International contact: Marjorie Rallins, Executive Director, Health Data Standards | [email removed]
